opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write (role does not own Payroll, so no admin). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB for E019 (Eric Woods): contractor, basic security training. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Contractor with basic training max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Ticket 1: Eric Woods (E019) requests write to Payroll. The Security note (looked up in own database) states E019 is a contractor with basic security training. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Engineer. Per policy, contractors max is read unless they have advanced security training (write); admin is never allowed. Since the requested write exceeds the contractor's maximum of read, grant read. The HR note claims full-time status, but given the conflicting employment-type information, the more restrictive, policy-compliant level is applied: read.
